questions.stem: What is the primary difference between a bad debt and a provision for doubtful debts?

options.text: Bad debt is an estimate, doubtful debt is confirmed.
Bad debt is confirmed, doubtful debt is an estimate.
Both are estimates of uncollectible debts.

questions.explanation: A bad debt is a confirmed irrecoverable amount, while a provision for doubtful debts is an estimate of potential future losses.

distractorRationale.a: This reverses the definitions of bad debts and doubtful debts.
distractorRationale.c: Only doubtful debts are estimates, not bad debts.
distractorRationale.d: Bad debts are confirmed, doubtful debts are not.

questions.stem: If a business writes off a bad debt of ₦20,000, what is the correct journal entry?

options.text: Debit Accounts Receivable ₦20,000; Credit Bad Debt Expense ₦20,000.
Debit Bad Debt Expense ₦20,000; Credit Accounts Receivable ₦20,000.

questions.explanation: The correct entry for writing off a bad debt is to debit Bad Debt Expense and credit Accounts Receivable.

distractorRationale.a: This reverses the debit and credit accounts.
distractorRationale.c: Cash is not involved in writing off a bad debt.

questions.stem: A business estimates its doubtful debts to be 5% of its ₦200,000 accounts receivable. What is the provision for doubtful debts?
questions.explanation: 5% of ₦200,000 is ₦10,000, which is the estimated provision for doubtful debts.

distractorRationale.a: This is calculated as 0.5% instead of 5%.
distractorRationale.c: This is 10% of the accounts receivable, not 5%.
distractorRationale.d: This is 10% of the accounts receivable, not 5%.

questions.stem: A provision for doubtful debts is recorded as an expense on the income statement.
questions.explanation: Provisions for doubtful debts are recorded as expenses because they represent estimated future losses.

distractorRationale.b: This is incorrect as provisions for doubtful debts are indeed recorded as expenses.

questions.stem: Explain how an increase in the provision for doubtful debts affects the financial statements of a business.
markingGuide: Identify that an increase in provision is recorded as an expense.
Explain that this reduces net income on the income statement.
Mention that it increases the provision for doubtful debts on the balance sheet.
questions.explanation: An increase in the provision for doubtful debts is recorded as an expense, reducing net income. It also increases the liability or reserve on the balance sheet, reflecting potential future losses.
